title: Shuffle and simulate
description:
Using the drill's generator (include your own copy of it), write:

```c
void shuffle(int *a, size_t n, Rng *r);                 /* Fisher-Yates, from the end */
double estimate_pi(Rng *r, long samples);               /* 4 x (share of random points inside the quarter circle) */
int birthday_share(Rng *r, int people, int trials);     /* in how many of the trials do two of the people share a birthday (365 days) */
```

- `shuffle` goes from `i = n` down to 2, swapping `a[i - 1]` with `a[rng_below(r, i)]`. The tests check the exact result for a seed, so follow this order.
- `estimate_pi` takes two `rng_double` values per sample, `x` first.
- `birthday_share` gives each person `rng_below(r, 365)` and checks for any repeat.
hints: Fisher-Yates only ever picks from the positions not yet fixed: `j` from 0 to `i - 1` (lesson 8.06).
For birthdays, a `seen[365]` array cleared for each trial finds the first repeat; 23 people share a birthday about half the time.
